skills.name: benchmarking
skills.description: Guide for building, running, and analyzing Nanvix performance benchmarks. Use this when asked about benchmark setup, execution, or interpretation.

skills.name: build
skills.description: Guide for building, formatting, linting, and spell-checking Nanvix with z. Use this when asked to build or validate the repository.

skills.name: ci-cd-pipeline
skills.description: Guide for Nanvix CI and GitHub Actions workflow behavior, including local pipeline execution and matrix coverage. Use this when asked about CI checks, workflow failures, or release flow.

skills.name: coding-standards
skills.description: Detailed Nanvix coding, documentation, and review standards across Rust, C/C++, Python, and Shell. Use this when asked to implement or review code quality conventions.

skills.name: daemon-development
skills.description: Guide for developing and debugging Nanvix daemons, including guest daemons and host linuxd behavior. Use this when asked about daemon architecture or daemon changes.

skills.name: gdb-debugging
skills.description: Guide for debugging Nanvix guests using GDB remote debugging over the microvm machine type. Use this when asked about attaching GDB, setting breakpoints, or stepping through kernel code.

skills.name: kernel-development
skills.description: Guide for modifying and debugging the Nanvix kernel architecture and kernel-call paths. Use this when asked about kernel internals or kernel implementation changes.

skills.name: library-development
skills.description: Guide for creating and modifying Nanvix libraries under src/libs, including guest no_std and host std crates. Use this when asked about library architecture or crate changes.

skills.name: test-development
skills.description: Guide for writing, running, and debugging Nanvix unit, integration, and system tests in Rust and C/C++. Use this when asked about test implementation or failures.

skills.name: test
skills.description: Guide for running Nanvix tests with z. Use this when asked to run unit tests, integration tests, or the full test suite.

skills.name: troubleshooting
skills.description: Guide for diagnosing Nanvix build, runtime, and test failures, including cleanup and debugging workflows. Use this when asked to investigate errors or unstable behavior.

skills.name: user-app-development
skills.description: Guide for developing, building, and running Nanvix user-space applications across supported runtimes and languages. Use this when asked about guest app implementation or execution.

skills.name: find-skills
skills.description: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.

skills.name: customize-cloud-agent
skills.description: Skill for customizing the Copilot cloud agent (formerly known as Copilot coding agent) environment, including copilot-setup-steps.yml configuration, preinstalling tools and dependencies, runners, and settings. Use when the user mentions copilot-setup-steps, copilot setup steps, or wants to configure the cloud agent environment.

result.content:
1. # View Design: `mm::phys::frame`
2. 
3. > **Re-run after rollback (specification → view-design, attempt 1/1).**
4. > The previous design modeled the global frame-allocator singleton with an
5. > **argument-free, uninterpreted constant** `phys_view() -> PhysMemView`. A
6. > constant has the same value at every program point, so it cannot distinguish the
7. > pre- and post-state of a *mutating* operation. The specification phase proved
8. > (reproducers `02`/`03`) that, under the only sound single-state `instance()`
9. > bridge, asserting a **post-state** allocation fact over that constant is not
10. > merely unproven but **provably false** (it contradicts `FrameAllocView::wf`
11. > disjointness). The mutating shims were therefore forced to weaken to *pre-state*
12. > facts, contradicting the documented caller expectations.
13. >
14. > **This revision fixes the View's *state-threading mechanism*, not its abstract
15. > content.** The abstract content (`FrameAllocView` = allocated/free sets +
16. > refcount map) is already correct and is on the do-not-modify list; it is
17. > reproduced here for reference and **kept verbatim**. What changes is *how the
18. > current value of the singleton is exposed to a verified shim*: the 0-ary constant
19. > `phys_view()` is replaced by a **tracked authority token** whose `&mut` carries
20. > the `old → post` transition. This is the "standard Verus pattern for global
21. > mutable state" named in the rollback report (option 2).
22. 
23. ---
24. 
25. ## Abstract Resource
26. 
27. To callers, `frame` is **the system's single global pool of physical page
28. frames**: a fixed universe of page-aligned physical addresses partitioned into
29. *allocated* vs *free*, with a per-frame *reference count* layered on top so a
30. frame can be shared (copy-on-write) and is returned to the free pool only when
31. its last reference is released. Callers reach it through `pub(super)` free
32. functions over a singleton; they never see the backing bitmap or the BSS
33. refcount array.
34. 
35. The abstraction has two layers and (this revision) one mechanism layer:
36. 
37. 1. **`FrameAllocView`** — the abstract reservation state of the allocator
38.    (allocated set, free set, refcount map). *Do-not-modify; kept verbatim.*
39. 2. **`PhysMemView`** — the singleton's abstract value: a boot `initialized`
40.    lifecycle gate plus the `FrameAllocView`. *Kept; transition helpers extended.*
41. 3. **`PhysAuth` (NEW, tracked)** — the *carrier* of the current `PhysMemView`
42.    value. Replaces the 0-ary `phys_view()` constant so that a `&mut PhysAuth`
43.    exposes `old(auth)@` (pre) and `auth@` (post) of a mutation. This is the
44.    diff-able mechanism; it carries no new caller-observable *content*.
45. 
46. ---
47. 
48. ## View Struct
49. 
50. ### Allocator reservation state — `FrameAllocView` (do-not-modify; verbatim)
51. 
52. ```rust
53. pub struct FrameAllocView {
54.     /// Page-aligned physical addresses currently reserved (handed out or booked).
55.     pub allocated_frames: Set<int>,
56.     /// Page-aligned physical addresses currently available for allocation.
57.     pub free_frames: Set<int>,
58.     /// Maps each allocated frame address to its reference count.
59.     /// A frame is present in the map iff it is currently allocated. Value in 1..=255.
60.     pub refcounts: Map<int, int>,
61. }
62. ```
63. 
64. ### Singleton abstract value — `PhysMemView` (kept)
65. 
66. ```rust
67. pub struct PhysMemView {
68.     /// Boot lifecycle gate: `false` before `init`, `true` after a successful
69.     /// `init`. Models "initialized-before-use"; `instance()` panics if false.
70.     pub initialized: bool,
71.     /// The global allocator's reservation state. Well-formed once initialized.
72.     pub frames: FrameAllocView,
73. }
74. ```
75. 
76. ### Diff-able carrier — `PhysAuth` (NEW, tracked)
77. 
78. ```rust
79. /// Tracked ghost authority over the global frame-allocator singleton.
80. ///
81. /// Its abstract value is the current `PhysMemView`. Exactly one `PhysAuth`
82. /// exists (minted by `init`, thereafter held by `PhysMemoryManager`); holding
83. /// `&mut PhysAuth` is the right to mutate the singleton and, crucially, exposes
84. /// BOTH the pre-state `old(auth)@` and the post-state `auth@` of that mutation.
85. ///
86. /// `PhysAuth` adds NO new caller-visible content: `auth@` ranges over the SAME
87. /// `PhysMemView` values the previous design used. It only restores the ability
88. /// to *name two program points*, which a 0-ary spec constant cannot.
89. pub tracked struct PhysAuth { /* opaque ghost state */ }
90. 
91. impl PhysAuth {
92.     /// The singleton's abstract value at the current program point.
93.     pub spec fn view(self) -> PhysMemView;   //  auth@
94. }
95. ```
96. 
97. All caller-visible state is expressed in **mathematical types** (`Set<int>`,
98. `Map<int,int>`, `bool`) over **physical addresses** — never machine types, bit
99. indices, or pointers. `PhysAuth` is `tracked` (ghost): it is erased at runtime
100. and exists only to thread the abstract value across a mutation.
101. 
102. ---
103. 
104. ## Well-formedness Invariant
105. 
106. ```rust
107. // FrameAllocView::wf  (do-not-modify; reproduced verbatim for reference)
108. pub open spec fn wf(&self) -> bool {
109.     &&& forall|addr: int| self.allocated_frames.contains(addr) ==> addr % spec_page_size() == 0
110.     &&& forall|addr: int| self.free_frames.contains(addr) ==> addr % spec_page_size() == 0
111.     &&& self.allocated_frames.disjoint(self.free_frames)
112.     &&& forall|addr: int| #[trigger] self.allocated_frames.contains(addr) <==>
113.             self.refcounts.contains_key(addr) && self.refcounts[addr] > 0
114.     &&& forall|addr: int| #[trigger] self.free_frames.contains(addr) ==>
115.             !self.refcounts.contains_key(addr)
116.     &&& forall|addr: int| self.refcounts.contains_key(addr) ==>
117.             0 < self.refcounts[addr] <= 255
118. }
119. 
120. // PhysMemView::inv  (kept)
121. pub open spec fn inv(self) -> bool {
122.     self.initialized ==> self.frames.wf()
123. }
124. ```
125. 
126. These encode exactly the caller-perspective facts from the analysis: the
127. **partition** (disjoint, page-aligned), the **refcount coupling**
128. (`allocated ⟺ refcount > 0`; free frames have no entry), the **u8 bound**
129. (`0 < c ≤ 255`), and **initialized-before-use**. No bitmap/array clause leaks
130. into `wf`; the implementation-coupling invariant lives in the do-not-modify
131. `Inner::internal_inv`.
132. 
133. The `PhysAuth` carrier needs no new well-formedness of its own beyond
134. `auth@.inv()`: it is a faithful holder of a `PhysMemView`, and its `inv()` is
135. just `self.view().inv()`.
136. 
137. ---
138. 
139. ## Spec Transition Functions
140. 
141. The mutating operations are expressed as **transitions on `PhysMemView`** (a pure
142. function `old_view → new_view`). The previous design already defined
143. `spec_initialize`, `spec_book_frame`, and `spec_book_frames`; this revision adds
144. the per-operation transitions the mutating shims need so they can write
145. `auth@ == old(auth)@.spec_<op>(...)` against the *post* state. All live on the
146. `PhysMemView` type (a View artifact), never as extra `pub spec fn`s on `Inner`.
147. 
148. ```rust
149. impl PhysMemView {
150.     // ----- Derived predicates (methods, NOT fields — see Rejected Alternatives) -----
151.     pub open spec fn covered(self) -> Set<int> {
152.         self.frames.allocated_frames.union(self.frames.free_frames)
153.     }
154.     pub open spec fn region_frames(start: int, size: int) -> Set<int> {
155.         let first = start / spec_page_size();
156.         let last  = (start + size) / spec_page_size();
157.         set_int_range(first, last).map(|i: int| i * spec_page_size())
158.     }
159. 
160.     // ----- Lifecycle -----
161.     pub open spec fn spec_initialize(self, initial: FrameAllocView) -> PhysMemView {
162.         PhysMemView { initialized: true, frames: initial }
163.     }
164. 
165.     // ----- Reservation: free -> allocated, refcount := 1 -----
166.     /// `alloc` / `book`: a single free frame becomes allocated with one reference.
167.     pub open spec fn spec_alloc_one(self, addr: int) -> PhysMemView {
168.         PhysMemView {
169.             frames: FrameAllocView {
170.                 allocated_frames: self.frames.allocated_frames.insert(addr),
171.                 free_frames:      self.frames.free_frames.remove(addr),
172.                 refcounts:        self.frames.refcounts.insert(addr, 1int),
173.             },
174.             ..self
175.         }
176.     }
177.     // `spec_book_frame` is retained as the existing name/alias of `spec_alloc_one`.
178. 
179.     /// `alloc_contiguous` / `alloc_range`: a whole set moves free -> allocated,
180.     /// each with refcount 1. (Generalizes a contiguous run to an arbitrary set.)
181.     pub open spec fn spec_alloc_set(self, frames: Set<int>) -> PhysMemView {
182.         PhysMemView {
183.             frames: FrameAllocView {
184.                 allocated_frames: self.frames.allocated_frames.union(frames),
185.                 free_frames:      self.frames.free_frames.difference(frames),
186.                 refcounts:        self.frames.refcounts.union_prefer_right(
187.                     Map::new(|a: int| frames.contains(a), |a: int| 1int)),
188.             },
189.             ..self
190.         }
191.     }
192.     // `spec_book_frames` is retained as the existing name/alias of `spec_alloc_set`.
193. 
194.     // ----- Reference counting -----

382.   `alloc_contiguous`, `book`, `alloc_range`, `share`, `refcount` reasons about
383.   "the frame is now / still in `allocated_frames`". *Substitution:* any allocator
384.   must know which frames it has handed out. ✅ Addresses (not bit indices) because
385.   callers hold `FrameAddress` and compare via `frame@`.

394.   pin `refcounts[f] == 1`. *Substitution:* reference-counted shared ownership is a

 > `UserFrame`/`KernelFrame` and consumed in `Drop` (the Rc-style refcount pattern).
 > That is a larger, optional refinement; it is **not** needed to satisfy any
 > documented caller, so it is left out to keep the change minimal.
 
 ---
 
 ## Design Rationale (per field, with substitution test)
 
 > Substitution test: *"If the implementation were completely rewritten with a
 > different algorithm (free-list, buddy allocator, B-tree of extents…), would
 > this field still make sense?"*
 
 - **`FrameAllocView.allocated_frames: Set<int>`** — every caller of `alloc`,
   `alloc_contiguous`, `book`, `alloc_range`, `share`, `refcount` reasons about
   "the frame is now / still in `allocated_frames`". *Substitution:* any allocator
   must know which frames it has handed out. ✅ Addresses (not bit indices) because
   callers hold `FrameAddress` and compare via `frame@`.
 
 - **`FrameAllocView.free_frames: Set<int>`** — `alloc`/`book`/`alloc_range`
   require the target be *in* `free_frames`; `free_count`'s watermark gate reasons
   over it; the partition invariant needs it. *Substitution:* "which frames are
   available" is intrinsic to any allocator. ✅
 
 - **`FrameAllocView.refcounts: Map<int,int>`** — `share` (+1), `free` (−1, release
   at 0), and `refcount` (exact value) are *defined* by this map; fresh allocations
   pin `refcounts[f] == 1`. *Substitution:* reference-counted shared ownership is a
   behavioral contract, not an implementation choice. ✅ Keyed by address, present
   **iff** allocated (doubles as the allocated-set witness via `wf`).
 
 - **`PhysMemView.initialized: bool`** — every shim except `init` requires it;
   `instance()` panics otherwise; `free`-from-`Drop` must preserve `inv()` gated on
   it. *Substitution:* a one-shot boot gate is inherent to a process-wide singleton.
   ✅
 
 - **`PhysMemView.frames: FrameAllocView`** — composes the allocator state into the
   singleton value. *Substitution:* a singleton is "lifecycle + the resource it
   guards". ✅
 
 - **`PhysAuth` (carrier, tracked) — passes the substitution test as a *mechanism*,
   not content.** It stores no algorithm-specific data; its `view()` is a
   `PhysMemView`. *Substitution:* **any** implementation of a mutable global
   singleton, under **any** allocation algorithm, needs a way for a verified mutator
   to name the post-state — a threaded ghost token is the algorithm-independent way
   to do that. ✅ It is the *correct* generalization of the rejected 0-ary constant,
   which failed precisely because it pretended a mutable singleton could be named
   without threading.

 | **No code-as-spec** | Transitions are set/map rewrites (`insert`/`remove`/`union`/`difference`), never bitmap scans. WHAT, not HOW. ✅ |
 | **Sound** | No spec constant is asked to hold two values; `instance()` carries no contradictory `ensures`; `free` keeps a *true* (weak) contract. No false axiom. ✅ |

 - **0-ary `uninterp spec fn phys_view() -> PhysMemView` (the attempt-1 design).**
   A constant cannot name pre- and post-state of a mutation; under the only sound
   `instance()` bridge a post-state membership `ensures` is **provably false**
   (reproducer `02`), and strengthening the bridge derives `false` (reproducer
   `03`). This is the defect being fixed. ❌
 
 - **A *pair* of 0-ary constants `phys_view_pre()` / `phys_view_post()`.** Lets a
   *single* shim state a transition, but cannot **sequence**: the `post` of one
   operation must equal the `pre` of the next, which two constants cannot express
   (they would have to be globally equal, collapsing them). Unsound/unusable for
   `book(a); book(b)` chains at the manager level. ❌ (Threading a token is the only
   form of "pre/post pair" that sequences — hence `PhysAuth`.)
 
 - **Strengthening `instance()`'s `external_body` `ensures` to reflect post-state
   into the constant.** Forces `pre == post` for any mutation, i.e. an inconsistent
   (false) axiom on a trusted accessor — strictly worse than `admit`. ❌
 
 - **Per-handle `Tracked<FrameRef>` permission for *every* operation (full Rc-style
   refcount state machine).** The most precise model (would let even `free` express
   its exact transition by consuming the handle's reference token in `Drop`). But it
   requires adding a `tracked` field to the `UserFrame`/`KernelFrame` exec structs
   and changing `free`'s signature — large, invasive, and **unnecessary**: no
   documented caller needs `free`'s precise transition. Recorded as a future
   refinement, not adopted. ❌ (for now)
 
 - **Bitmap as `Seq<bool>` / bit-vector keyed by frame *number*.** Mirrors the
   concrete `Bitmap`; fails substitution (a free-list/buddy allocator has no bits);
   callers hold addresses, not indices. ❌
 
 - **A `free_count: usize`/`nat` field.** Derivable as `free_frames.len()` (with
   `.finite()`); the watermark caller reasons over the set directly. ❌ (kept as a
   derivation).
 
 - **A `covered: Set<int>` field.** Equal to `allocated ∪ free`; provided as the
   `covered()` method so `is_covered`'s contract reads naturally without a synced
   field. ❌ as a field, ✅ as a helper.

   reasoning; the `≤ 255` bound is in `wf`. ❌

   derivable, but kept explicit so `wf` makes the equivalence a trigger-friendly
   fact and the bulk transitions read as symmetric `union`/`difference`. A
   deliberate, invariant-pinned minimal redundancy. ✅ keep.
 
 - **Folding `initialized` into `FrameAllocView`.** The boot gate belongs to the
   *singleton*, not to reservation state; separating it keeps `FrameAllocView`
   reusable. ✅ two-layer split.

13. pub uninterp spec fn byte_at_address(ptr: int) -> u8;

15. /// Abstract view of the frame allocator (`frame::Inner`).
16. ///
17. /// Captures which physical frames are currently allocated vs. free,
18. /// together with a per-frame reference count that models shared
19. /// ownership (e.g. copy-on-write after `share()`).
20. pub struct FrameAllocView
21. {
22.     pub allocated_frames: Set<int>,
23.     pub free_frames: Set<int>,
24.     /// Maps each allocated frame address to its reference count.
25.     /// A frame is present in the map iff it is currently allocated.
26.     pub refcounts: Map<int, int>,
27. }
28. 
29. impl FrameAllocView
30. {
31.     pub open spec fn wf(&self) -> bool
32.     {
33.         // Page-alignment
34.         &&& forall|addr: int| self.allocated_frames.contains(addr) ==> addr % spec_page_size() == 0
35.         &&& forall|addr: int| self.free_frames.contains(addr) ==> addr % spec_page_size() == 0
36.         // Disjoint
37.         &&& self.allocated_frames.disjoint(self.free_frames)
38.         // Allocated ↔ refcount consistency: a frame is allocated iff it has a positive refcount
39.         &&& forall|addr: int| #[trigger] self.allocated_frames.contains(addr) <==>
40.             self.refcounts.contains_key(addr) && self.refcounts[addr] > 0
41.         // Free frames have no refcount entry
42.         &&& forall|addr: int| #[trigger] self.free_frames.contains(addr) ==>
43.             !self.refcounts.contains_key(addr)
44.         // Refcount bounded by u8 range
45.         &&& forall|addr: int| self.refcounts.contains_key(addr) ==>
46.             0 < self.refcounts[addr] <= 255
47.     }
48. }

86. ///
87. /// Models the boot lifecycle of the frame-allocator singleton plus its
88. /// frame-reservation state. The `frames` component mirrors `frame::instance()@`;
89. /// the `initialized` flag mirrors the `INSTANCE_INIT` lifecycle gate.
90. pub struct PhysMemView {
91.     /// Whether the frame-allocator singleton has been established
92.     /// (i.e. `init` ran once and returned `Ok`). Models one-shot/monotonic
93.     /// boot: `false` before `init`, `true` after a successful `init`.
94.     pub initialized: bool,

96.     /// frames are reserved (allocated) vs. free, with per-frame refcounts.

99. }

102.     /// Well-formedness: once the allocator is established, the frame-allocator
103.     /// invariant holds. Before initialization there is no allocator, so no
104.     /// constraint applies.
105.     pub open spec fn inv(self) -> bool {

114. 
115.     /// The set of frame addresses occupied by a region `[start, start+size)`.
116.     pub open spec fn region_frames(start: int, size: int) -> Set<int> {
117.         let first = start / spec_page_size();
118.         let last = (start + size) / spec_page_size();
119.         set_int_range(first, last).map(|i: int| i * spec_page_size())
120.     }
121. 
122.     /// `init` established the allocator from the caller-supplied bitmap state;
123.     /// lifecycle flips on.
124.     pub open spec fn spec_initialize(self, initial: FrameAllocView) -> PhysMemView {
125.         PhysMemView { initialized: true, frames: initial }
126.     }
127. 
128.     /// Book one covered frame: move `addr` from free to allocated, refcount = 1.
129.     /// Mirrors `Inner::book`'s `Ok` post-state.
130.     pub open spec fn spec_book_frame(self, addr: int) -> PhysMemView {
131.         PhysMemView {
132.             frames: FrameAllocView {
133.                 allocated_frames: self.frames.allocated_frames.insert(addr),
134.                 free_frames: self.frames.free_frames.remove(addr),
135.                 refcounts: self.frames.refcounts.insert(addr, 1int),
136.             },
137.             ..self
138.         }
139.     }
140. 
141.     /// Book a set of frames at once: move them all from free to allocated, each
142.     /// with refcount = 1. Mirrors `Inner::alloc_range`'s `Ok` post-state and
143.     /// generalizes it from a contiguous region to an arbitrary frame set.
144.     pub open spec fn spec_book_frames(self, frames: Set<int>) -> PhysMemView {
145.         PhysMemView {
146.             frames: FrameAllocView {
147.                 allocated_frames: self.frames.allocated_frames.union(frames),
148.                 free_frames: self.frames.free_frames.difference(frames),
149.                 refcounts: self.frames.refcounts.union_prefer_right(
150.                     Map::new(|a: int| frames.contains(a), |a: int| 1int),
151.                 ),
152.             },
153.             ..self
154.         }
155.     }
156. }
157. 
158. /// Abstract view of the global physical-memory subsystem at the current program
159. /// point.
160. ///
161. /// The subsystem state lives in module-level `static`s (`frame::INSTANCE` /
162. /// `frame::INSTANCE_INIT`) that a Verus `spec fn` cannot read directly, so this
163. /// is an *uninterpreted* function: the exec wrappers in `frame.rs` and the
164. /// `book_*`/`init` functions pin down its value through their `ensures` clauses.
165. /// `initialized` mirrors `INSTANCE_INIT`; `frames` mirrors `frame::instance()@`.
166. ///
167. /// This is the handle the caller-facing contract of `init` is stated over: after
168. /// a successful `init`, `phys_view().initialized` and `phys_view().inv()` hold, so
169. /// every later `frame::*` / `PhysMemoryManager::*` operation may rely on the
170. /// frame-allocator invariant.
171. pub uninterp spec fn phys_view() -> PhysMemView;
172. 
173. } // end verus!

620. // Use relaxed ordering for all atomic operations to mitigate synchronization overhead. It is safe
621. // to use this ordering semantics because Nanvix is a single-core system, and the kernel runs with
622. // interrupts disabled.
623. const ORDER: Ordering = Ordering::Relaxed;
624. 
625. //==================================================================================================
626. // Singleton
627. //==================================================================================================
628. 
629. /// Module-level singleton storage.
630. static mut INSTANCE: MaybeUninit<Inner> = MaybeUninit::uninit();
631. 
632. /// Whether the frame allocator has been initialized.
633. static INSTANCE_INIT: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);
634. 
635. /// Returns a mutable reference to the initialized singleton.
636. //
637. // Trust boundary (see `verus-ai-logs/tcb-allowed.md`): `instance` reads the
638. // module-level `static mut INSTANCE` / `INSTANCE_INIT` through
639. // `unsafe { INSTANCE.assume_init_mut() }`. A Verus `spec fn` cannot read those
640. // statics, and the verifier does not support `static mut` paths, so the bridge
641. // between the live singleton and the uninterpreted `phys_view()` is asserted
642. // here as an external contract: once the allocator is initialized, the returned
643. // reference is well-formed and its abstract view equals `phys_view().frames`.
644. #[verus_verify(external_body)]
645. #[verus_spec(result =>
646.     requires
647.         phys_view().initialized,
648.     ensures
649.         (*result).inv(),
650.         (*result)@ == phys_view().frames,
651. )]
652. fn instance() -> &'static mut Inner {
653.     if unlikely(!INSTANCE_INIT.load(ORDER)) {
654.         panic!("frame allocator used before init()");
655.     }
656. 
657.     // SAFETY: `INSTANCE_INIT` is `true`, so `INSTANCE` has been fully written by `init()`.
658.     // The kernel is single-threaded with interrupts disabled, so no concurrent access is possible.
659.     unsafe { INSTANCE.assume_init_mut() }
660. }
661. 
662. //==================================================================================================
663. // Public Free Functions
664. //==================================================================================================
665. 
666. /// Initialize the frame allocator singleton.
667. ///
668. /// # Safety
669. ///
670. /// Must be called exactly once during boot, before any other function
671. /// in this module.
672. //
673. // Skip/exclude from the proof target (see `verus-ai-logs/tcb-allowed.md`): `init`
674. // materializes the `&'static mut [u8]` refcount table from `static mut
675. // REFCOUNT_STORAGE` and writes the `static mut INSTANCE`, neither of which the
676. // verifier supports. Its `#[verus_spec]` contract is honored as a trust boundary.
677. #[verus_verify(external_body)]
678. #[verus_spec(result =>
679.     ensures
680.         // `init` establishes the subsystem invariant. On success the allocator is
681.         // marked initialized; on either outcome the abstract view is well-formed
682.         // (vacuously so if it never became initialized).
683.         phys_view().inv(),
684.         match result {
685.             Ok(()) => phys_view().initialized,
686.             Err(_) => true,
687.         },
688. )]
689. pub(super) unsafe fn init(bitmap: Bitmap) -> Result<(), Error> {
690.     if unlikely(INSTANCE_INIT.load(ORDER)) {
691.         return Err(Error::new(ErrorCode::InvalidArgument, "frame allocator already initialized"));
692.     }
693. 
694.     info!(
695.         "frame allocator: {} frames, {} MB",
696.         bitmap.number_of_bits(),
697.         (bitmap.number_of_bits() * mem::FRAME_SIZE) / constants::MEGABYTE,
698.     );
699. 
700.     let nframes: usize = bitmap.number_of_bits();
701.     if nframes > NFRAMES {
702.         return Err(Error::new(
703.             ErrorCode::InvalidArgument,
704.             "frame bitmap is larger than the configured refcount storage",
705.         ));
706.     }
707. 
708.     // SAFETY: single-threaded boot; no other reference to `REFCOUNT_STORAGE` exists.
709.     let refcount: &'static mut [u8] = unsafe { &mut REFCOUNT_STORAGE[..] };
710. 
711.     // Defensively sync refcounts with any bits already set in the incoming bitmap. The
712.     // current microvm boot path supplies an empty bitmap and performs all reservations
713.     // via `book()` / `alloc_range()` after `init()`, so this loop normally does nothing.
714.     // It is kept as a safety net so a future boot path that hands us a pre-populated
715.     // bitmap (for example to express firmware-reserved regions) does not silently end
716.     // up with `bitmap bit = 1, refcount = 0`, which would cause the first `free()` of
717.     // such a frame to be rejected as a spurious double-free.
718.     for (i, slot) in refcount.iter_mut().enumerate().take(nframes) {
719.         if matches!(bitmap.test(i), Ok(true)) {
720.             *slot = 1;
721.         }
722.     }
723. 
724.     // SAFETY: single-threaded boot; no other reference to `INSTANCE` exists.
725.     unsafe { INSTANCE.write(Inner { bitmap, refcount }) };
726.     INSTANCE_INIT.store(true, ORDER);
727.     Ok(())
728. }
729. 
730. /// Allocate a frame.
731. #[verus_spec(result =>
732.     requires
733.         phys_view().initialized,
734.         phys_view().inv(),
735.     ensures
736.         phys_view().inv(),
737.         phys_view().initialized,
738.         // As with the other mutating shims, the post-state membership effect (the
739.         // frame now being in `allocated_frames` with refcount 1) is not expressible
740.         // against the fixed pre-state `phys_view()` (no `old(phys_view())` to diff;
741.         // see `alloc_contiguous`/`book` and bugs.md). The sound, verified facts are
742.         // that a successful result is a well-formed (page-aligned) frame address and
743.         // that it was free in the pool immediately before the call.
744.         match result {
745.             Ok(frame) => {
746.                 &&& frame.inv()
747.                 &&& phys_view().frames.free_frames.contains(frame@)
748.             },
749.             Err(_) => true,
750.         },
751. )]
752. pub(super) fn alloc() -> Result<FrameAddress, Error> {
753.     instance().alloc()
754. }
755. 
756. /// # Description
757. ///
758. /// Allocates `count` physically contiguous frames.
759. ///
760. /// # Returns
761. ///
762. /// Returns the base `FrameAddress` of the contiguous range.
763. ///
764. #[verus_spec(result =>
765.     requires
766.         phys_view().initialized,
767.         phys_view().inv(),
768.         count > 0,
769.     ensures
770.         phys_view().inv(),
771.         phys_view().initialized,
772.         // As with `alloc`, the post-state contiguity/membership effect over the
773.         // freshly reserved range is not expressible against the fixed pre-state
774.         // `phys_view()` (see `alloc` and bugs.md). The sound, verified facts are
775.         // that a successful result is a well-formed base address and that the
776.         // `count` page-strided frames it spans were all free immediately before
777.         // the call (contiguity precondition for identity-mapped kernel stacks).
778.         match result {
779.             Ok(base) => {
780.                 &&& base.inv()
781.                 &&& Set::new(|addr: int|
782.                     exists|i: int| 0 <= i < count
783.                         && addr == #[trigger] (base@ + i * spec_page_size())
784.                 ).subset_of(phys_view().frames.free_frames)
785.             },
786.             Err(_) => true,
787.         },
788. )]
789. pub(super) fn alloc_contiguous(count: usize) -> Result<FrameAddress, Error> {
790.     instance().alloc_contiguous(count)
791. }
792. 
793. ///
794. /// # Description
795. ///
796. /// Returns the number of free frames in the system.
797. ///
798. /// # Returns
799. ///
800. /// The number of free frames in the system.
801. ///
802. #[verus_spec(result =>
803.     requires
804.         phys_view().initialized,
805.         phys_view().inv(),
806.     ensures
807.         phys_view().inv(),
808.         phys_view().initialized,
809.         // Pure query: returns the size of the free pool. The free set is finite
810.         // (it is carved from the finite bitmap), which the watermark caller
811.         // (`check_user_watermark`) relies on to reason with `spec_watermark_ok`.
812.         phys_view().frames.free_frames.finite(),
813.         result as int == phys_view().frames.free_frames.len(),
814. )]
815. pub(super) fn free_count() -> usize {
816.     let inner = instance();
817.     // VERUS DEVIATION (pre-approved: intermediate value for assertions):
818.     // `number_of_bits() - usage()` is split into named bindings so the proof can
819.     // recover `num_bits >= 0` from the `usize` result of `number_of_bits()`.
820.     // `Bitmap::inv()` references the bitmap's private backing slice, so the bound
821.     // is opaque in this module and cannot be derived inside `lemma_free_count`.
822.     let nbits: usize = inner.bitmap.number_of_bits();
823.     let used: usize = inner.bitmap.usage();
824.     proof! {
825.         lemma_free_count(inner);
826.     }
827.     nbits - used
828. }
829. 
830. /// Free a frame previously returned by [`alloc`].
831. #[verus_spec(result =>
832.     ensures
833.         // `free` runs on `Drop` of any `UserFrame`/`KernelFrame`, so it carries no
834.         // caller precondition. It preserves the subsystem invariant on every path
835.         // (releasing a reference, and the last reference returns the frame to the
836.         // free pool). The exact refcount transition is not expressible here:
837.         // `phys_view()` is a single fixed value, with no `old(phys_view())` to
838.         // compare against.
839.         phys_view().inv(),
840.     // `free` is invoked from `Drop` impls (`UserFrame`/`KernelFrame`), which are
841.     // `no_unwind` and `opens_invariants none`; the shim honours both: it opens no
842.     // verifier invariants and cannot unwind (errors are returned as values).
843.     opens_invariants none
844.     no_unwind
845. )]
846. pub(super) fn free(frame: FrameAddress) -> Result<(), Error> {
847.     // `free` is reached from `Drop`, where the global allocator's `initialized`
848.     // precondition required by `instance()` is not locally re-established (there is
849.     // no `old(phys_view())` and no ghost token threaded through `Drop`). Honoring
850.     // the `no_unwind` contract for the panic-free path is a proving-phase
851.     // obligation, deferred here. The spec itself (`phys_view().inv()` preserved) is
852.     // sound; see `verus-ai-logs/nanvix-phys-phys-frame/bugs.md`.
853.     proof! {
854.         admit();
855.     }
856.     instance().free(frame)
857. }
858. 
859. ///
860. /// # Description
861. ///
862. /// Checks whether the frame allocator tracks the frame at the given physical address.
863. ///
864. /// # Returns
865. ///
866. /// Returns `true` when the frame allocator tracks the frame at `phys_addr`.
867. ///
868. #[verus_spec(ret =>
869.     requires
870.         phys_view().initialized,
871.         phys_addr.inv(),
872.     ensures
873.         phys_view().inv(),
874.         // `is_covered` reports exactly the frames the allocator tracks: the union
875.         // of reserved and free frames (`PhysMemView::covered`).
876.         ret <==> phys_view().covered().contains(phys_addr@),
877. )]
878. pub(super) fn is_covered(phys_addr: PageAligned<PhysicalAddress>) -> bool {
879.     instance().is_covered(phys_addr)
880. }
881. 
882. /// Reserve a frame so [`alloc`] will skip it.
883. #[verus_spec(result =>
884.     requires
885.         phys_view().initialized,
886.         phys_addr.inv(),
887.     ensures
888.         phys_view().inv(),
889.         // On success the booked frame was free immediately before the call; on
890.         // failure it was not free. The post-state effect (the frame now being in
891.         // `allocated_frames`) is not expressible against the fixed pre-state
892.         // `phys_view()` (see `alloc` and bugs.md).
893.         phys_view().initialized,
894.         match result {
895.             Ok(()) => phys_view().frames.free_frames.contains(phys_addr@),
896.             Err(_) => !phys_view().frames.free_frames.contains(phys_addr@),
897.         },
898. )]
899. pub(super) fn book(phys_addr: PageAligned<PhysicalAddress>) -> Result<(), Error> {
900.     instance().book(phys_addr)
901. }
902. 
903. /// Book every frame in the given physical memory region.
904. #[verus_spec(result =>
905.     requires
906.         phys_view().initialized,
907.         region.inv(),
908.     ensures
909.         phys_view().inv(),
910.         phys_view().initialized,
911.         // On success every frame of the region was free immediately before the
912.         // call; on failure at least one was not free. The region's frame set is
913.         // `PhysMemView::region_frames`, matching `Inner::alloc_range`. The
914.         // post-state effect (the frames now being allocated) is not expressible
915.         // against the fixed pre-state `phys_view()` (see `alloc` and bugs.md).
916.         match result {
917.             Ok(()) => PhysMemView::region_frames(region@.start, region@.size)
918.                 .subset_of(phys_view().frames.free_frames),
919.             Err(_) => !PhysMemView::region_frames(region@.start, region@.size)
920.                 .subset_of(phys_view().frames.free_frames),
921.         },
922. )]
923. pub(super) fn alloc_range(region: &TruncatedMemoryRegion<PhysicalAddress>) -> Result<(), Error> {
924.     instance().alloc_range(region)
925. }
926. 
927. /// Add a new reference to an already-allocated frame (e.g. for copy-on-write sharing).
928. #[verus_spec(result =>
929.     requires
930.         phys_view().initialized,
931.         phys_view().inv(),
932.         frame.inv(),
933.     ensures
934.         phys_view().inv(),
935.         phys_view().initialized,
936.         // On success the frame remains allocated (it has gained a reference). The
937.         // increment itself is not stated: `phys_view()` is a single fixed value
938.         // with no `old(phys_view())` to compare against.
939.         match result {
940.             Ok(()) => {
941.                 &&& phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(frame@)
942.                 &&& phys_view().frames.refcounts.contains_key(frame@)
943.             },
944.             Err(_) => !phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(frame@)
945.                 || (phys_view().frames.refcounts.contains_key(frame@)
946.                     && phys_view().frames.refcounts[frame@] >= 255),
947.         },
948. )]
949. pub(super) fn share(frame: FrameAddress) -> Result<(), Error> {
950.     instance().share(frame)
951. }
952. 
953. /// Returns the current reference count of an already-allocated frame.
954. #[verus_spec(result =>
955.     requires
956.         phys_view().initialized,
957.         phys_view().inv(),
958.         frame.inv(),
959.     ensures
960.         phys_view().inv(),
961.         phys_view().initialized,
962.         // A pure query: on success it returns the frame's current refcount (and
963.         // the frame is allocated); on failure the frame is not allocated.
964.         match result {
965.             Ok(count) => {
966.                 &&& phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(frame@)
967.                 &&& phys_view().frames.refcounts.contains_key(frame@)
968.                 &&& count as int == phys_view().frames.refcounts[frame@]
969.             },
970.             Err(_) => !phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(frame@),
971.         },
972. )]
973. pub(super) fn refcount(frame: FrameAddress) -> Result<u8, Error> {
974.     instance().refcount(frame)
975. }

215.         if count == 0 {
216.             return Ok(());
217.         }
218. 
219.         Self::check_user_watermark(count)?;
220. 
221.         for _ in 0..count {
222.             match self.upool.alloc() {
223.                 Ok(frame) => frames.push(frame),
224.                 Err(error) => {
225.                     frames.clear();
226.                     return Err(error);
227.                 },
228.             }
229.         }
230.         Ok(())
231.     }
232. 
233.     ///
234.     /// # Description
235.     ///
236.     /// Allocates a single user frame, applying the same kernel watermark check as
237.     /// [`Self::alloc_many_user_frames`]. This is the single-frame fast path used on
238.     /// hot paths such as copy-on-write fault resolution, where allocating an
239.     /// intermediate [`Vec`] would be wasteful.
240.     ///
241.     /// # Returns
242.     ///
243.     /// Upon success, a [`UserFrame`] is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned
244.     /// instead.
245.     ///
246.     // Trusted shim: applies the watermark gate then delegates to the global
247.     // `Upool::alloc`. On success the returned frame's physical address is now in
248.     // the allocator's `allocated_frames` and is page-aligned.
249.     #[verus_verify(external_body)]
250.     #[verus_spec(result =>
251.         requires
252.             phys_view().initialized,
253.             phys_view().inv(),
254.         ensures
255.             phys_view().inv(),
256.             phys_view().initialized,
257.             match result {
258.                 Ok(frame) => {
259.                     &&& phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(frame@)
260.                     &&& frame@ % spec_page_size() == 0
261.                     &&& phys_view().frames.free_frames.finite()
262.                     &&& spec_watermark_ok(phys_view().frames, 0)
263.                 },
264.                 Err(_) => true,
265.             },
266.     )]
267.     pub fn alloc_user_frame(&mut self) -> Result<UserFrame, Error> {
268.         Self::check_user_watermark(1)?;
269.         self.upool.alloc()
270.     }
271. 
272.     ///
273.     /// # Description
274.     ///
275.     /// Rejects user allocations of `count` frames that would breach the kernel
276.     /// watermark, i.e. that would drop the number of free frames below
277.     /// [`config::kernel::KERNEL_WATERMARK`].
278.     ///
279.     /// # Parameters
280.     ///
281.     /// - `count`: Number of user frames the caller intends to allocate.
282.     ///
283.     /// # Returns
284.     ///
285.     /// Upon success, `Ok(())` is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
286.     ///
287.     // Trusted shim: reads the global free-frame count and compares it against
288.     // `KERNEL_WATERMARK + count`. Pure gate, no allocator state change. `Ok` exactly
289.     // captures the watermark policy: at least `KERNEL_WATERMARK` frames remain free
290.     // after servicing `count`. `Err` covers both the overflow guard and a breach.
291.     #[cfg_attr(verus_keep_ghost, allow(verus_impl_method_marker))]
292.     #[verus_verify(external_body)]
293.     #[verus_spec(result =>
294.         requires
295.             phys_view().initialized,
296.             phys_view().inv(),
297.         ensures
298.             phys_view().inv(),
299.             phys_view().initialized,
300.             phys_view().frames.free_frames.finite(),
301.             match result {
302.                 Ok(()) => spec_watermark_ok(phys_view().frames, count as int),
303.                 Err(_) => true,
304.             },
305.     )]
306.     fn check_user_watermark(count: usize) -> Result<(), Error> {
307.         let watermark_threshold: usize = config::kernel::KERNEL_WATERMARK
308.             .checked_add(count)
309.             .ok_or_else(|| {
310.                 let reason: &str = "watermark + count overflow";
311.                 error!("{reason}");
312.                 Error::new(ErrorCode::InvalidArgument, reason)
313.             })?;
314.         if frame::free_count() < watermark_threshold {
315.             let reason: &str = "would breach kernel watermark";
316.             error!("{reason}");
317.             return Err(Error::new(ErrorCode::OutOfMemory, reason));
318.         }
319.         Ok(())
320.     }
321. 
322.     ///
323.     /// # Description
324.     ///
325.     /// Allocates a kernel frame.
326.     ///
327.     /// Kernel allocations bypass the watermark — no artificial ceiling.
328.     ///
329.     /// # Return Values
330.     ///
331.     /// Upon success, a kernel frame is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
332.     ///
333.     // Trusted shim: allocates one frame from the global allocator (bypassing the
334.     // watermark) and wraps it, freeing the raw frame if wrapping fails. On success
335.     // the returned frame's base address is now allocated and page-aligned.
336.     #[verus_verify(external_body)]
337.     #[verus_spec(result =>
338.         requires
339.             phys_view().initialized,
340.             phys_view().inv(),
341.         ensures
342.             phys_view().inv(),
343.             phys_view().initialized,
344.             match result {
345.                 Ok(frame) => {
346.                     &&& phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(frame@)
347.                     &&& frame@ % spec_page_size() == 0
348.                 },
349.                 Err(_) => true,
350.             },
351.     )]
352.     pub fn alloc_kernel_frame(&mut self) -> Result<KernelFrame, Error> {
353.         let frame_addr: FrameAddress = frame::alloc()?;
354.         KernelFrame::new(frame_addr).inspect_err(|e| {
355.             warn!("failed to wrap frame after KernelFrame::new failure: {e:?}");
356.             if let Err(free_err) = frame::free(frame_addr) {
357.                 warn!("failed to free frame after KernelFrame::new failure: {free_err:?}");
358.             }
359.         })
360.     }
361. 
362.     ///
363.     /// # Description
364.     ///
365.     /// Allocates a contiguous range of kernel frames into caller-provided storage.
366.     ///
367.     /// Kernel stacks require physically contiguous frames because the kernel uses identity
368.     /// mapping and the hardware stack pointer traverses the region linearly.
369.     /// Kernel allocations bypass the watermark — no artificial ceiling.
370.     ///
371.     /// # Parameters
372.     ///
373.     /// - `count`: Number of frames to allocate.
374.     /// - `frames`: Mutable reference to a pre-allocated vector into which to store
375.     ///   those frames' addresses.
376.     ///
377.     /// # Return Values
378.     ///
379.     /// Upon success, `Ok(())` is returned and `frames` is filled with `count`
380.     /// contiguous entries. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
381.     ///
382.     // Trusted shim: allocates a physically-contiguous run from the global allocator
383.     // (bypassing the watermark) and wraps each frame, with a two-phase
384.     // (`Vec::clear` + `frame::free`) rollback Verus cannot body-verify without
385.     // editing exec code. On success exactly `count` frames are handed out, each now
386.     // allocated, and their base addresses form an ascending page-stride run
387.     // (contiguity is load-bearing for kernel stacks). On error the vector is emptied.
388.     #[verus_verify(external_body)]
389.     #[verus_spec(result =>
390.         requires
391.             phys_view().initialized,
392.             phys_view().inv(),
393.             old(frames)@.len() == 0,
394.         ensures
395.             phys_view().inv(),
396.             phys_view().initialized,
397.             match result {
398.                 Ok(()) => {
399.                     &&& final(frames)@.len() == count
400.                     &&& forall|i: int|
401.                         0 <= i < count as int ==>
402.                             #[trigger] phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(final(frames)@[i]@)
403.                     &&& exists|base: int|
404.                         #[trigger] kernel_frames_contiguous(final(frames)@, base)
405.                 },
406.                 Err(_) => final(frames)@.len() == 0,
407.             },
408.     )]
409.     pub fn alloc_many_kernel_frames(
410.         &mut self,
411.         count: usize,
412.         frames: &mut Vec<KernelFrame>,
413.     ) -> Result<(), Error> {
414.         // Check if caller-provided vector is not empty.
415.         if !frames.is_empty() {
416.             let reason: &str = "frames vector is not empty";
417.             error!("{reason}");
418.             return Err(Error::new(ErrorCode::InvalidArgument, reason));
419.         }
420.         if frames.capacity() < count {
421.             let reason: &str = "frames vector has insufficient capacity";
422.             error!("{reason}");
423.             return Err(Error::new(ErrorCode::InvalidArgument, reason));
424.         }
425. 
426.         let base_addr: FrameAddress = frame::alloc_contiguous(count)?;
427.         let base_raw: usize = base_addr.into_raw_value();
428.         for i in 0..count {
429.             let raw_addr: usize = base_raw + i * mem::PAGE_SIZE;
430.             match FrameAddress::from_raw_value(raw_addr).and_then(KernelFrame::new) {
431.                 Ok(kf) => frames.push(kf),
432.                 Err(e) => {
433.                     // Drop already-wrapped frames (frees them via KernelFrame::Drop).
434.                     frames.clear();
435.                     // Free remaining un-wrapped frames from the contiguous allocation.
436.                     for j in i..count {
437.                         let leak_raw: usize = base_raw + j * mem::PAGE_SIZE;
438.                         if let Ok(fa) = FrameAddress::from_raw_value(leak_raw) {
439.                             if let Err(e) = frame::free(fa) {
440.                                 warn!("failed to free leaked frame {fa:?}: {e:?}");
441.                             }
442.                         }
443.                     }
444.                     return Err(e);
445.                 },
446.             }
447.         }
448.         Ok(())
449.     }
450. }
451.

contradictory—a freshly allocated frame can't simultaneously satisfy
the pre-state invariant at that single program point. The reproducer seems to demonstrate this is prov

analysis.

the reviewer actually withdrew that concern in Turn
2 and accepted these external_body axioms as tcb-allowed, so I can keep the manager as-is.
The real deliverable is strengthening `Upool::alloc` from its weak postcondition `
Ok ⇒ free_frames.contains(uf@)` to the stronger `allocated_frames.contains(uf@) && refcounts[uf@]==1`, which
means threading a carrier through the frame allocation call.
The carrier
flows from `frame::alloc(token)` producing a strong postcondition on the token, which `
Upool::alloc` then forwards and states. Since `Upool::alloc` takes `&mut self` with no fields
, the token comes as a `with Tracked(auth)` parameter, and its caller in manager (the external_body) just calls the tokenless version. The key
question is whether to keep `phys_view()` in the requires or switch entirely
to the carrier — I can tie them with `old(auth)@ == phys_view()`, but that's
a requirement the caller must establish. Actually, the carrier might be self-sufficient on its own:
`old(auth)@.initialized && old(auth)@.inv()` as requires, with instance() bridging `(*r)@ == auth@.frames`, so I may
not need `phys_view()` in the carrier path at all.
But
`instance()` currently has both a tokenless contract using `phys_view()` and would
need a token-carrying version, which creates a problem:
if both describe `(*r)@`, they implicitly force `auth@.frames == phys_view().frames`.
The cleanest approach is to make the token version of `instance()` drop `
phys_view()` entirely and use only the carrier. However, `instance()` also serves `
free()`, which can't thread a token through the Drop path, so I need both a tokenless and token
version. With the `with` clause, the tokenless version becomes `requires false`, but `free()` currently has `admit()` and
the reviewer wants that removed — so if `free()` calls `instance()` and `instance()` now
requires a token, I'm stuck.
The alternative
is to keep `instance()` as-is without adding a token, then in the mutating shim, after calling `instance().alloc()`, re-sync the token from
the result in a ghost block. This requires the precondition that `old(auth)@ == ph
ys_view()` (since `instance()` gives `old(r)@ == phys_view().frames`), which ensures the token and the
frame state stay consistent through the allocation and re-sync.
For
the query shims, I should add `Tracked(&PhysAuth)` as the reviewer requested, even
though they don't mutate — it's a polish that makes the interface more uniform
The
hard verification gate is clear: zero errors, admit=0 for frame.rs,
Upool::alloc with the strong post-state, and the build succeeds. The per-shim strengthening is part of the fix request, so
I'll thread the carrier through all mutating shims (alloc, alloc_contiguous, book, alloc_range,
share) and add Tracked params to the query shims where it helps cleanly.
The tr
icky part is removing admit from frame::free—it currently relies on instance() which requires phys_view().initialized, but free has
no precondition to establish that. I need to either avoid calling instance() in free or
find another way to satisfy its precondition.
The
real issue is that instance() requires initialized, but free() has no precondition to prove it. I could
remove instance()'s requires and make the ensures conditional on initialized —
the panic path diverges anyway, so the postcondition only matters when the function actually returns. But
Verus's external_body doesn't automatically model panic divergence, so I'd need to handle that
carefully.
Actually
, the reviewer said I can modify instance() since
it's in the verification target. The cleanest approach might be to give free() a
contract with `opens_invariants none, no_unwind` and ensure the physical view's invariant holds,
then have the body call instance() — but I still need to resolve how
instance() gets called without its precondition being met.
If
I redefine instance() to require nothing and conditionally ensure the invariant holds
only when initialized, then free() can call it, but free() still can't satisfy Inner
::free's precondition without knowing the allocator is initialized. This exposes a real soundness issue: free
is undefined behavior if the allocator wasn't initialized, so the admit was hiding
a legitimate gap. The honest fix would be to encode the initialized guarantee
into UserFrame's type invariant itself, but that's a larger refactor
than what the reviewer is asking for.
Re
-reading the feedback though, the reviewer is open to changing free's ensures to something "Drop-compatible and always-true that verifies cleanly."
The real constraint is the body—instance() and Inner::free's
preconditions. What if I restructure instance() to unconditionally ensure the invariant holds
? Since instance() panics if uninitialized, any return path means the Inner is valid, so `
ensures (*result).inv()` without a requires clause would be sound. The tricky part is keeping the frames
postcondition while managing the initialized dependency.
instance
() isn't on the do-not-modify list and view_design.md explicitly redesigns it, so I can change its
contract. Dropping the `requires phys_view().initialized` means all callers would
get that as an ensure instead, which is fine since they already
require it. The soundness concern is that if instance() panics when not initialized, the ensures only
hold on the return path, which Verus treats as valid since the diverging path never
reaches the ensures.
So
my plan is to remove the requires from instance() and add an ensures for `phys_view().initialized`, then
check whether FrameAddress.inv() needs establishing in free(). Before
diving into the full implementation, I should verify this approach by checking the inv
() implementations and testing incrementally—starting with mod.spec.rs and the Ph
ysAuth transitions, then frame::alloc in isolation.

data.reasoningText:
I'm seeing the core issue now: the reviewer's assertion that `phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(frame@)` must hold after allocation is actually contradictory—a freshly allocated frame can't simultaneously satisfy the pre-state invariant at that single program point. The reproducer seems to demonstrate this is provably false, though I'm questioning whether `phys_view()` being uninterpreted changes the analysis.

But the reviewer actually withdrew that concern in Turn 2 and accepted these external_body axioms as tcb-allowed, so I can keep the manager as-is. The real deliverable is strengthening `Upool::alloc` from its weak postcondition `Ok ⇒ free_frames.contains(uf@)` to the stronger `allocated_frames.contains(uf@) && refcounts[uf@]==1`, which means threading a carrier through the frame allocation call.

The carrier flows from `frame::alloc(token)` producing a strong postcondition on the token, which `Upool::alloc` then forwards and states. Since `Upool::alloc` takes `&mut self` with no fields, the token comes as a `with Tracked(auth)` parameter, and its caller in manager (the external_body) just calls the tokenless version. The key question is whether to keep `phys_view()` in the requires or switch entirely to the carrier — I can tie them with `old(auth)@ == phys_view()`, but that's a requirement the caller must establish. Actually, the carrier might be self-sufficient on its own: `old(auth)@.initialized && old(auth)@.inv()` as requires, with instance() bridging `(*r)@ == auth@.frames`, so I may not need `phys_view()` in the carrier path at all.

But `instance()` currently has both a tokenless contract using `phys_view()` and would need a token-carrying version, which creates a problem: if both describe `(*r)@`, they implicitly force `auth@.frames == phys_view().frames`. The cleanest approach is to make the token version of `instance()` drop `phys_view()` entirely and use only the carrier. However, `instance()` also serves `free()`, which can't thread a token through the Drop path, so I need both a tokenless and token version. With the `with` clause, the tokenless version becomes `requires false`, but `free()` currently has `admit()` and the reviewer wants that removed — so if `free()` calls `instance()` and `instance()` now requires a token, I'm stuck.

The alternative is to keep `instance()` as-is without adding a token, then in the mutating shim, after calling `instance().alloc()`, re-sync the token from the result in a ghost block. This requires the precondition that `old(auth)@ == phys_view()` (since `instance()` gives `old(r)@ == phys_view().frames`), which ensures the token and the frame state stay consistent through the allocation and re-sync.

For the query shims, I should add `Tracked(&PhysAuth)` as the reviewer requested, even though they don't mutate — it's a polish that makes the interface more uniform.

The hard verification gate is clear: zero errors, admit=0 for frame.rs, Upool::alloc with the strong post-state, and the build succeeds. The per-shim strengthening is part of the fix request, so I'll thread the carrier through all mutating shims (alloc, alloc_contiguous, book, alloc_range, share) and add Tracked params to the query shims where it helps cleanly.

The tricky part is removing admit from frame::free—it currently relies on instance() which requires phys_view().initialized, but free has no precondition to establish that. I need to either avoid calling instance() in free or find another way to satisfy its precondition. The real issue is that instance() requires initialized, but free() has no precondition to prove it. I could remove instance()'s requires and make the ensures conditional on initialized — the panic path diverges anyway, so the postcondition only matters when the function actually returns. But Verus's external_body doesn't automatically model panic divergence, so I'd need to handle that carefully.

Actually, the reviewer said I can modify instance() since it's in the verification target. The cleanest approach might be to give free() a contract with `opens_invariants none, no_unwind` and ensure the physical view's invariant holds, then have the body call instance() — but I still need to resolve how instance() gets called without its precondition being met.

If I redefine instance() to require nothing and conditionally ensure the invariant holds only when initialized, then free() can call it, but free() still can't satisfy Inner::free's precondition without knowing the allocator is initialized. This exposes a real soundness issue: free is undefined behavior if the allocator wasn't initialized, so the admit was hiding a legitimate gap. The honest fix would be to encode the initialized guarantee into UserFrame's type invariant itself, but that's a larger refactor than what the reviewer is asking for.

Re-reading the feedback though, the reviewer is open to changing free's ensures to something "Drop-compatible and always-true that verifies cleanly." The real constraint is the body—instance() and Inner::free's preconditions. What if I restructure instance() to unconditionally ensure the invariant holds? Since instance() panics if uninitialized, any return path means the Inner is valid, so `ensures (*result).inv()` without a requires clause would be sound. The tricky part is keeping the frames postcondition while managing the initialized dependency. instance() isn't on the do-not-modify list and view_design.md explicitly redesigns it, so I can change its contract. Dropping the `requires phys_view().initialized` means all callers would get that as an ensure instead, which is fine since they already require it. The soundness concern is that if instance() panics when not initialized, the ensures only hold on the return path, which Verus treats as valid since the diverging path never reaches the ensures.

So my plan is to remove the requires from instance() and add an ensures for `phys_view().initialized`, then check whether FrameAddress.inv() needs establishing in free(). Before diving into the full implementation, I should verify this approach by checking the inv() implementations and testing incrementally—starting with mod.spec.rs and the PhysAuth transitions, then frame::alloc in isolation.

40. #[derive(Debug)]
41. #[verus_verify]
42. pub struct KernelFrame {
43.     /// Frame address.
44.     base: FrameAddress,
45. }
46. 
47. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
48. verus! {
49. 
50. /// Abstract view of a [`KernelFrame`]: the base physical address of the frame it
51. /// owns. Lets allocator contracts name a returned kernel frame's address (e.g.
52. /// the contiguity guarantee of `alloc_many_kernel_frames`) without exposing any
53. /// storage detail.
54. impl View for KernelFrame {
55.     type V = int;
56. 
57.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> int {
58.         self.base@
59.     }
60. }
61. 
62. } // verus!
63. 
64. #[verus_verify]
65. impl KernelFrame {
66.     ///
67.     /// # Description
68.     ///
69.     /// Instantiates a kernel frame.
70.     ///
71.     /// # Parameters
72.     ///
73.     /// - `base`: Frame address.
74.     ///
75.     /// # Returns
76.     ///
77.     /// Upon success, a kernel frame is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
78.     ///
79.     #[verus_spec(result =>
80.         ensures
81.             // Address identity: on success the handle owns exactly the input
82.             // address, so callers can transfer the allocator facts established
83.             // for `base` (membership, alignment) onto the returned handle. On
84.             // failure no handle exists; `base` is `Copy`, so nothing is consumed
85.             // and the caller remains free to release the raw frame.
86.             match result {
87.                 Ok(frame) => frame@ == base@,
88.                 Err(_) => true,
89.             },
90.     )]
91.     pub(super) fn new(base: FrameAddress) -> Result<Self, Error> {
92.         // Ensure the frame is identity-mapped in the kernel address space so that
93.         // Deref/DerefMut can safely access it. This lazily installs a page
94.         // table entry if needed (page tables come from a BSS pool, so no recursive frame
95.         // allocation occurs).
96.         let phys_addr: PageAligned<PhysicalAddress> =
97.             PageAligned::from_raw_value(base.into_raw_value()).map_err(|e| {
98.                 error!("frame base is not page-aligned: {e:?}");
99.                 e
100.             })?;
101.         crate::mm::virt::identity_map_page(phys_addr).map_err(|e| {
102.             error!("failed to identity-map frame: {:?}", e);
103.             e
104.         })?;
105. 
106.         Ok(Self { base })
107.     }
108. 
109.     ///
110.     /// # Description
111.     ///
112.     /// Returns the base address of the target kernel frame.
113.     ///
114.     /// # Returns
115.     ///
116.     /// The base address of the target kernel frame.
117.     ///
118.     #[verus_spec(result =>
119.         ensures
120.             // Pure read: the returned address is the handle's abstract value.
121.             result@ == self@,
122.     )]
123.     pub fn base(&self) -> FrameAddress {
124.         self.base
125.     }
126. 
127.     ///
128.     /// # Description
129.     ///
130.     /// Clears the target kernel frame.
131.     ///
132.     /// Uses the identity-map `memset` backend so that the write runs in the kernel address space.
133.     /// This avoids a page fault when the current CR3 points to a user page directory that lacks
134.     /// the PDE for this frame's physical address.
135.     ///
136.     // Trusted (TCB, out of verification scope): materializes a `*mut u8` from the
137.     // frame's raw address (`usize as *mut u8`) and writes through the identity-map
138.     // `memset` backend -- a raw-memory operation Verus cannot model. Listed in
139.     // `verus-ai-logs/tcb-allowed.md`.
140.     #[verus_verify(external_body)]
141.     pub fn clear(&mut self) -> Result<(), Error> {
142.         let base: *mut u8 = self.base.into_raw_value() as *mut u8;
143.         crate::mm::virt::memset(base, 0, mem::PAGE_SIZE).map_err(|e| {
144.             error!("memset failed: {:?}", e);
145.             e
146.         })
147.     }
148. }
149. 
150. /// # Safety
151. ///
152. /// `Deref` accesses the identity-mapped frame directly. The caller must ensure that the current
153. /// CR3 points to a page directory that has the relevant PDE for this frame's physical address
154. /// (i.e., the kernel page directory, or a user page directory into which the PDE has been
155. /// propagated via [`sync_kernel_pdes`](crate::mm::virt::sync_kernel_pdes)). For CR3-agnostic
156. /// writes, prefer [`KernelFrame::clear()`] which uses the identity-map `memset` backend.
157. impl Deref for KernelFrame {
158.     type Target = [u8];
159. 
160.     fn deref(&self) -> &Self::Target {
161.         let ptr: usize = self.base.into_raw_value();
162.         unsafe { core::slice::from_raw_parts(ptr as *const u8, mem::PAGE_SIZE) }
163.     }
164. }
165. 
166. /// # Safety
167. ///
168. /// See [`Deref`] impl — the same CR3 invariant applies.
169. impl DerefMut for KernelFrame {
170.     fn deref_mut(&mut self) -> &mut Self::Target {
171.         let ptr: usize = self.base.into_raw_value();
172.         unsafe { core::slice::from_raw_parts_mut(ptr as *mut u8, mem::PAGE_SIZE) }
173.     }
174. }
175. 
176. #[verus_verify]
177. impl Drop for KernelFrame {
178.     #[verus_spec(
179.         ensures
180.             // Releasing the frame preserves the subsystem invariant (the last
181.             // reference returns the frame to the free pool). The precise refcount
182.             // transition is not expressible: `phys_view()` is a single fixed value
183.             // with no `old(phys_view())` to compare against. Errors are logged, not
184.             // propagated, so `drop` cannot unwind.
185.             phys_view().inv(),
186.         opens_invariants none
187.         no_unwind
188.     )]
189.     fn drop(&mut self) {
190.         if let Err(e) = super::frame::free(self.base) {
191.             error!("failed to free kernel frame: {:?}", e);
192.         }
193.     }
194. }

8. ## Ghost/Tracked Parameters (`with` clause)
9. 
10. Functions can accept ghost/tracked parameters invisible to non-Verus callers.
11. 
12. ### Declaring a function with ghost/tracked params
13. 
14. ```rust
15. #[verus_spec(ret =>
16.     with
17.         Tracked(y): Tracked<&mut u32>,
18.         Ghost(w): Ghost<u64>
19.             -> z: Ghost<u32>
20.     requires
21.         x < 100,
22.         *old(y) < 100,
23.     ensures
24.         *y == x,
25.         ret == x,
26.         z == x,
27. )]
28. fn test_mut_tracked(x: u32) -> u32 {
29.     proof!{ *y = x; }
30.     #[verus_spec(with |= Ghost(x))]
31.     x
32. }
33. ```
34. 
35. - The `with` clause declares ghost/tracked inputs and ghost outputs (`-> z: Ghost<u32>`).
36. - `#[verus_spec(with |= Ghost(x))]` on the return expression returns a ghost output.
37. 
38. ### Calling with ghost/tracked
39. 
40. Use `#[verus_spec(with ...)]` on the call expression:
41. 
42. ```rust
43. fn test_cal_mut_tracked(x: u32) {
44.     proof_decl!{
45.         let ghost mut z;
46.         let tracked mut y = 0u32;
47.         z = 0u32;
48.     }
49. 
50.     // On a let statement:
51.     #[verus_spec(with Tracked(&mut y), Ghost(0) => Ghost(z))]
52.     let _ = test_mut_tracked(0u32);
53. 
54.     // On a bare expression (wrap in parens):
55.     (#[verus_spec(with Tracked(&mut y), Ghost(0))]
56.     test_mut_tracked(0u32));
57. }
58. ```
59. 
60. ### How it works
61. 
62. `#[verus_spec(with ...)]` generates **two versions** of the function:
63. - A verified version (`_VERUS_VERIFIED_xxx`) with ghost/tracked parameters
64. - An unverified version (original signature) with `requires false`
65. 
66. `#[verus_spec(with ...)]` at the call site calls the verified version.
67. Without it, the unverified version is called — which has `requires false`,
68. so calling from verified code without the `with` annotation will fail.
69. 
70. Unverified code can call the original version normally:
71. 
72. ```rust
73. fn external_caller(x: u32) -> u32 {
74.     test_mut_tracked(1)  // calls unverified version, no with needed
75. }
76. ```
77. 
78. ### Compatibility limitation
79. 
80. `#[verus_spec(with ...)]` call-site syntax only works with exec functions
81. verified via `#[verus_spec]`. Using it to call an exec function defined
82. inside `verus! { }` will error: `cannot find function _VERUS_VERIFIED_xxx`.
83. 
84. Workaround: create a trusted wrapper:
85. 
86. ```rust
87. #[verus_verify(external_body)]
88. #[verus_spec(v =>
89.     with Tracked(perm): Tracked<&mut PointsTo<T>>
90.     requires
91.         old(perm).ptr() == ptr,
92.         old(perm).is_init(),
93.     ensures
94.         perm.ptr() == ptr,
95.         perm.is_uninit(),
96.         v == old(perm).value(),
97. )]
98. fn ptr_mut_read<'a, T>(ptr: *const T) -> T {
99.     vstd::raw_ptr::ptr_mut_read(ptr, Tracked::assume_new())
100. }
101. ```
102. 
103. ---
104. 
105. ## Dual-Mode Functions (exec → spec)

 ```rust
 #[verus_spec(ret =>
     with
         Tracked(y): Tracked<&mut u32>,
         Ghost(w): Ghost<u64>
             -> z: Ghost<u32>
     requires
         x < 100,
         *old(y) < 100,
     ensures
         *y == x,
         ret == x,
         z == x,
 )]
 fn test_mut_tracked(x: u32) -> u32 {
     proof!{ *y = x; }
     #[verus_spec(with |= Ghost(x))]
     x
 }
 ```
 
 - The `with` clause declares ghost/tracked inputs and ghost outputs (`-> z: Ghost<u32>`).
 - `#[verus_spec(with |= Ghost(x))]` on the return expression returns a ghost output.
 
 ### Calling with ghost/tracked
 
 Use `#[verus_spec(with ...)]` on the call expression:
 
 ```rust
 fn test_cal_mut_tracked(x: u32) {
     proof_decl!{
         let ghost mut z;
         let tracked mut y = 0u32;
         z = 0u32;
     }
 
     // On a let statement:
     #[verus_spec(with Tracked(&mut y), Ghost(0) => Ghost(z))]
     let _ = test_mut_tracked(0u32);
 
     // On a bare expression (wrap in parens):
     (#[verus_spec(with Tracked(&mut y), Ghost(0))]
     test_mut_tracked(0u32));
 }
 ```
 
 ### How it works
 
 `#[verus_spec(with ...)]` generates **two versions** of the function:
 - A verified version (`_VERUS_VERIFIED_xxx`) with ghost/tracked parameters
 - An unverified version (original signature) with `requires false`

 Without it, the unverified version is called — which has `requires false`,
 so calling from verified code without the `with` annotation will fail.
 
 Unverified code can call the original version normally:
 
 ```rust

     test_mut_tracked(1)  // calls unverified version, no with needed
 }
 ```

 `#[verus_spec(with ...)]` call-site syntax only works with exec functions
 verified via `#[verus_spec]`. Using it to call an exec function defined
 inside `verus! { }` will error: `cannot find function _VERUS_VERIFIED_xxx`.
 
 Workaround: create a trusted wrapper:

 ```rust
 #[verus_verify(external_body)]
 #[verus_spec(v =>
     with Tracked(perm): Tracked<&mut PointsTo<T>>
     requires
         old(perm).ptr() == ptr,
         old(perm).is_init(),

         perm.ptr() == ptr,
         perm.is_uninit(),
         v == old(perm).value(),
 )]

 }
 ```
