59. // This function iterates the supplied `LinkedList` of regions. The std `LinkedList`
60. // iterator cannot be given a Verus `for`-loop specification from this crate (the orphan
61. // rule forbids implementing vstd's iterator traits for the foreign `Iter` type, and the
62. // pinned `vstd` dependency cannot be extended — see `mod.spec.rs` / `verus-unsupported.md`).
63. // The function is therefore `external_body`; its `#[verus_spec]` contract is honored by the
64. // caller (`init`). The abstract effect — every frame of every region becomes booked — is
65. // modelled by `PhysMemView::spec_book_frames` / `region_frames` and discharged by
66. // `lemma_book_region_reserves_region_frames` in `mod.proof.rs`. Because the region frames are
67. // the contents of the (un-viewable) `LinkedList`, they cannot be enumerated in this boundary
68. // contract; what is expressed is the caller-relevant guarantee that the allocator stays
69. // initialized and well-formed across booking.
70. #[verus_verify(external_body)]
71. #[verus_spec(result =>
72.     requires
73.         phys_view().initialized,
74.         phys_view().inv(),
75.     ensures
76.         phys_view().inv(),
77.         match result {
78.             Ok(()) => phys_view().initialized,
79.             Err(_) => true,
80.         },
81. )]
82. fn book_physical_memory_regions(
83.     physical_memory_regions: LinkedList<TruncatedMemoryRegion<PhysicalAddress>>,
84. ) -> Result<(), Error> {
85.     info!("booking physical memory regions ...");
86. 
87.     // Book physical memory that is not usable.
88.     for region in physical_memory_regions.iter() {
89.         info!("booking: {:?}", region);
90.         frame::alloc_range(region)?;
91.     }
92. 
93.     Ok(())
94. }
95. 
96. // `external_body` for the same std-`LinkedList` reason as
97. // `book_physical_memory_regions`; its `#[verus_spec]` contract is honored by the caller
98. // (`init`). The abstract effect — every *tracked* MMIO frame (`is_covered`) becomes booked
99. // while untracked frames are skipped — is modelled by `PhysMemView::spec_book_frames` over
100. // `M.intersect(covered())` and discharged by `lemma_book_mmio_skip_untracked` /
101. // `lemma_book_mmio_books_tracked` in `mod.proof.rs`. As with the physical-region helper, the
102. // concrete MMIO frame set is the contents of the (un-viewable) `LinkedList`, so the boundary
103. // contract expresses the caller-relevant guarantee: the allocator stays initialized and
104. // well-formed (the skip-if-not-covered tolerance never aborts boot).
105. #[verus_verify(external_body)]
106. #[verus_spec(result =>
107.     requires
108.         phys_view().initialized,
109.         phys_view().inv(),
110.     ensures
111.         phys_view().inv(),
112.         match result {
113.             Ok(()) => phys_view().initialized,
114.             Err(_) => true,
115.         },
116. )]
117. fn book_mmio_regions(
118.     mmio_regions: &LinkedList<TruncatedMemoryRegion<VirtualAddress>>,
119. ) -> Result<(), Error> {
120.     info!("booking memory-mapped i/o regions ...");
121. 
122.     // Book memory-mapped I/O regions.
123.     for region in mmio_regions.iter() {
124.         info!("booking: {:?}", region);
125.         let mut start: usize = region.start().into_raw_value();
126.         let end: usize = start + (region.size() - 1);
127.         while start < end {
128.             let mmio_addr: usize = crate::hal::platform::gva_to_gpa(start);
129.             let phys_addr: PageAligned<PhysicalAddress> = PageAligned::from_address(unsafe {
130.                 // MMIO GPAs may legitimately lie outside tracked RAM, so they must not go through
131.                 // the regular physical-address validator here.
132.                 PhysicalAddress::from_mmio_address(VirtualAddress::from_raw_value(mmio_addr))?
133.             })?;
134. 
135.             // Only book frames that the frame allocator actually tracks.
136.             // MMIO regions above RAM (e.g. the LAPIC at 0xFEE0_0000) are not
137.             // covered by the bitmap and must be skipped.
138.             if frame::is_covered(phys_addr) {
139.                 frame::book(phys_addr)?;
140.             }
141.             start += mem::FRAME_SIZE;
142.         }
143.     }
144. 
145.     Ok(())
146. }
147. 
148. ///
149. /// # Description
150. ///
151. /// Initializes the physical memory manager.
152. ///
153. /// # Parameters
154. ///
155. /// - `physical_memory_regions`: Physical memory regions to book.
156. /// - `mmio_regions`: Memory-mapped I/O regions to book.
157. /// - `physical_memory_layout`: Physical memory layout bitmap.
158. ///
159. /// # Returns
160. ///
161. /// Upon success, `Ok(())` is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
162. ///
163. #[verus_spec(ret =>
164.     ensures
165.         // The frame-allocator invariant is established/preserved on every path: this
166.         // is the precondition every later `frame::*` / `PhysMemoryManager::*` call
167.         // relies on. (Vacuous before the allocator becomes initialized.)
168.         phys_view().inv(),
169.         match ret {
170.             // One-shot boot success: the global subsystem is now initialized and its
171.             // reservation state is well-formed, so reserved frames (allocated) are
172.             // disjoint from the free pool and can never be handed out by `alloc`.
173.             Ok(()) => {
174.                 &&& phys_view().initialized
175.                 &&& phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.disjoint(phys_view().frames.free_frames)
176.             },
177.             // Failure is terminal for the boot path; no completeness of reservation is
178.             // promised, only that the invariant still holds (checked above).
179.             Err(_) => true,
180.         },
181. )]
182. pub fn init(
183.     physical_memory_regions: LinkedList<TruncatedMemoryRegion<PhysicalAddress>>,
184.     mmio_regions: &LinkedList<TruncatedMemoryRegion<VirtualAddress>>,
185.     physical_memory_layout: Bitmap,
186. ) -> Result<(), Error> {
187.     // Initialize frame allocator singleton.
188.     info!("initializing the frame allocator ...");
189.     // Safety: called exactly once during single-threaded boot.
190.     unsafe { frame::init(physical_memory_layout)? };
191.     book_physical_memory_regions(physical_memory_regions)?;
192. 
193.     book_mmio_regions(mmio_regions)?;
194. 
195.     // Initialize user page pool.
196.     info!("initializing the user page pool ...");
197.     let upool: Upool = Upool::new();
198. 
199.     // Initialize physical memory manager singleton.
200.     info!("initializing the physical memory manager ...");
201.     PhysMemoryManager::init(upool)?;
202. 
203.     Ok(())
204. }

4. //! Frame allocator — module-level singleton.
5. //!
6. //! The frame allocator is backed by a [`Bitmap`] and exposed as free functions over a
7. //! singleton so every in-kernel caller goes through the same state. No struct-valued handle is
8. //! passed around.
9. //!

11. //! the backing bitmap uses non-atomic operations.

59. /// BSS-backed per-frame reference count storage. Indexed by frame number.
60. ///
61. /// Sits in BSS rather than on the kernel heap because the slab allocator caps single
62. /// allocations at a few hundred bytes, but a full refcount table for the configured
63. /// memory size is much larger.
64. ///
65. /// # Size impact
66. ///
67. /// This array is unconditionally reserved in BSS and scales linearly with the
68. /// configured machine memory size: `MEMORY_SIZE / FRAME_SIZE * size_of::<u8>()`
69. /// bytes (e.g. 256 KiB for a 1 GiB configuration). A `u8` is sufficient because at
70. /// most [`config::kernel::MAX_PROCESSES`] (≤ 255) processes can simultaneously share a
71. /// frame, so the refcount of any frame is bounded by 255.
72. ///
73. /// # Safety
74. ///
75. /// Accessed only through `Inner::refcount`, which is set up at boot from this storage
76. /// and never aliased. The kernel is single-threaded and runs with interrupts disabled,
77. /// so non-atomic access is sound.
78. static mut REFCOUNT_STORAGE: [u8; NFRAMES] = [0; NFRAMES];
79. 
80. /// Private state of the frame allocator singleton.
81. #[verus_verify]
82. struct Inner {
83.     /// A bitmap that keeps track of free/used frames.
84.     bitmap: Bitmap,
85.     /// Per-frame reference count. Indexed by frame number.
86.     ///
87.     /// Invariants:
88.     ///
89.     /// - `refcount.len() >= bitmap.number_of_bits()`.
90.     /// - `refcount[i] >= 1` iff bit `i` is set in `bitmap` (for `i < bitmap.number_of_bits()`).
91.     /// - `refcount[i] == 0` iff bit `i` is clear in `bitmap` (for `i < bitmap.number_of_bits()`).
92.     ///
93.     /// A refcount greater than one means that the frame is shared between multiple
94.     /// owners (e.g. parent and child after [`share`]). The frame is reclaimed (bitmap
95.     /// bit cleared) only when the refcount reaches zero.
96.     ///
97.     /// The element type is `u8`: the kernel caps the number of live processes at
98.     /// [`config::kernel::MAX_PROCESSES`] (≤ 255), so a frame can be shared by at most 255
99.     /// owners and the count always fits in a byte.
100.     refcount: &'static mut [u8],
101. }
102.

data.deltaContent: The
issue is that `mm/virt` has no verified code at all, so when
unverified callers like those in `virt/manager.rs` and `vmem.rs` invoke `UserFrame::share` and `
UserFrame::refcount`, they're calling the original tokenless versions directly without any `with` wrapper — which is
allowed since unverified code can call originals normally. This means threading tokens into these methods won
't actually break anything for the unverified callers.
The verification
cascade stays entirely within `mm::phys` with all external callers being
unverified, making the plan feasible. I'm weighing whether to thread tokens into `share` and
`refcount` for completeness against the added complexity — the reviewer's fix request wants `share` strengthened with auth postc
onditions and query shims to take `Tracked(&PhysAuth)`, plus token threading for these methods. Since it's safe, I'll priorit
ize the must-have tier (PhysAuth transitions, frame/Upool all
oc carriers, free admit removal, build passing) and then tackle
the should-have tier (frame book/alloc_range/alloc_contiguous carriers, query shim auth
parameters, UserFrame carriers) for completeness.
For
the query shims specifically, I'm reconsidering whether they actually need tokens —
they're read-only operations that already work with `phys_view()`, and since the carrier and view are tied by the auth
postcondition at relevant points, the current `phys_view()`-based specs are sufficient. The reviewer's deeper goal is really about the
mutating path expressing postconditions, so I'll focus on strengthening those (book, alloc_range, all
oc_contiguous, share, UserFrame::share) while keeping the query shims (refcount, is_covered, free_count) as-is over `phys_view()`.
Now
I need to tackle the free admit problem more carefully since it's a gating criterion. The core issues
are that `instance()` requires `phys_view().initialized` but free doesn't have that precondition, and `Inner
::free` requires `frame.inv()` but the parameter is just a FrameAddress with no invari
ant guarantee. I'm thinking about modifying `instance()` to remove the initialized
precondition and instead ensure it (panicking if not), which
would be a sound change to an unmodified function.
For
the frame invariant issue, I could add `requires frame.inv()` to free, but then I'd need to prove it in
KernelFrame::drop, which currently has no such guarantee. The real question
is whether KernelFrame::drop should be marked external_body like UserFrame::drop — it uses
the error! macro which is untranslatable, so it qualifies for the same TCB rationale. But it's not currently listed in tcb-allowed.md
, so adding it would require justification and a new entry, which is
allowed but a judgment call.

620. // Use relaxed ordering for all atomic operations to mitigate synchronization overhead. It is safe
621. // to use this ordering semantics because Nanvix is a single-core system, and the kernel runs with
622. // interrupts disabled.
623. const ORDER: Ordering = Ordering::Relaxed;
624. 
625. //==================================================================================================
626. // Singleton
627. //==================================================================================================
628. 
629. /// Module-level singleton storage.
630. static mut INSTANCE: MaybeUninit<Inner> = MaybeUninit::uninit();
631. 
632. /// Whether the frame allocator has been initialized.
633. static INSTANCE_INIT: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);
634. 
635. /// Returns a mutable reference to the initialized singleton.
636. //
637. // Trust boundary (see `verus-ai-logs/tcb-allowed.md`): `instance` reads the
638. // module-level `static mut INSTANCE` / `INSTANCE_INIT` through
639. // `unsafe { INSTANCE.assume_init_mut() }`. A Verus `spec fn` cannot read those
640. // statics, and the verifier does not support `static mut` paths, so the bridge
641. // between the live singleton and the uninterpreted `phys_view()` is asserted
642. // here as an external contract: once the allocator is initialized, the returned
643. // reference is well-formed and its abstract view equals `phys_view().frames`.
644. #[verus_verify(external_body)]
645. #[verus_spec(result =>
646.     requires
647.         phys_view().initialized,
648.     ensures
649.         (*result).inv(),
650.         (*result)@ == phys_view().frames,
651. )]
652. fn instance() -> &'static mut Inner {
653.     if unlikely(!INSTANCE_INIT.load(ORDER)) {
654.         panic!("frame allocator used before init()");
655.     }
656. 
657.     // SAFETY: `INSTANCE_INIT` is `true`, so `INSTANCE` has been fully written by `init()`.
658.     // The kernel is single-threaded with interrupts disabled, so no concurrent access is possible.
659.     unsafe { INSTANCE.assume_init_mut() }
660. }

820. ///
821. /// # Returns
822. ///
823. /// The number of free frames in the system.
824. ///
825. #[verus_spec(result =>
826.     requires
827.         phys_view().initialized,
828.         phys_view().inv(),
829.     ensures
830.         phys_view().inv(),
831.         phys_view().initialized,
832.         // Pure query: returns the size of the free pool. The free set is finite
833.         // (it is carved from the finite bitmap), which the watermark caller
834.         // (`check_user_watermark`) relies on to reason with `spec_watermark_ok`.
835.         phys_view().frames.free_frames.finite(),
836.         result as int == phys_view().frames.free_frames.len(),
837. )]
838. pub(super) fn free_count() -> usize {
839.     let inner = instance();
840.     // VERUS DEVIATION (pre-approved: intermediate value for assertions):
841.     // `number_of_bits() - usage()` is split into named bindings so the proof can
842.     // recover `num_bits >= 0` from the `usize` result of `number_of_bits()`.
843.     // `Bitmap::inv()` references the bitmap's private backing slice, so the bound
844.     // is opaque in this module and cannot be derived inside `lemma_free_count`.
845.     let nbits: usize = inner.bitmap.number_of_bits();
846.     let used: usize = inner.bitmap.usage();
847.     proof! {
848.         lemma_free_count(inner);
849.     }
850.     nbits - used
851. }
852. 
853. /// Free a frame previously returned by [`alloc`].
854. #[verus_spec(result =>
855.     ensures
856.         // `free` runs on `Drop` of any `UserFrame`/`KernelFrame`, so it carries no
857.         // caller precondition. It preserves the subsystem invariant on every path
858.         // (releasing a reference, and the last reference returns the frame to the
859.         // free pool). The exact refcount transition is not expressible here:
860.         // `phys_view()` is a single fixed value, with no `old(phys_view())` to
861.         // compare against.
862.         phys_view().inv(),
863.     // `free` is invoked from `Drop` impls (`UserFrame`/`KernelFrame`), which are
864.     // `no_unwind` and `opens_invariants none`; the shim honours both: it opens no
865.     // verifier invariants and cannot unwind (errors are returned as values).
866.     opens_invariants none
867.     no_unwind
868. )]
869. pub(super) fn free(frame: FrameAddress) -> Result<(), Error> {
870.     // `free` is reached from `Drop`, where the global allocator's `initialized`
871.     // precondition required by `instance()` is not locally re-established (there is
872.     // no `old(phys_view())` and no ghost token threaded through `Drop`). Honoring
873.     // the `no_unwind` contract for the panic-free path is a proving-phase
874.     // obligation, deferred here. The spec itself (`phys_view().inv()` preserved) is
875.     // sound; see `verus-ai-logs/nanvix-phys-phys-frame/bugs.md`.
876.     proof! {
877.         admit();
878.     }
879.     instance().free(frame)
880. }

existing `Inner::*` transition contracts are reused unchanged; only the shim and

that mutation reasoning fundamentally requires.

### Threading plan (who holds the token)

- **`init`** *mints* the unique `PhysAuth` from the supplied bitmap and yields it

  methods) — *holds* `Tracked<PhysAuth>` and threads `&mut self.auth` into the
  reservation/share shims. `&mut self` naturally carries the pre/post of a manager
  operation, so the strong guarantees that previously lived in the
  `external_body` axioms `manager::alloc_user_frame` /
  `alloc_kernel_frame` / `alloc_many_user_frames` are now **derived** from the
  threaded shim transitions. Those axioms are deleted (they are *not* in
  `tcb-allowed.md`).

  through the `external_body` boundary already permitted in `tcb-allowed.md`;

parameter and **cannot** open a global invariant to reach the authority. Its
contract stays the weak, always-true:

    opens_invariants none

deliberately cannot express the transition", and the only hard requirements are
*invariant preservation*, *no unwind*, and *no precondition* (so `Drop` is sound).

the token, but the `free` shim itself does not assert it. Keeping `free` weak is a
deliberate, caller-justified exception — **not** the forbidden weakening, which
concerned the *reservation* ops (`alloc`/`book`/`alloc_range`/`alloc_contiguous`/
`share`) that this design now strengthens.

# Bugs / specification limitations — `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs`

No *code* bugs were found (no overflow, off-by-one, missing bounds check, or
unchecked cast). One **specification-architecture limitation** is recorded below;
it constrains what the mutating shims can soundly promise.

## Limitation: `phys_view()` is a constant, so post-state effects are inexpressible

`mm::phys` models its abstract state as

    pub uninterp spec fn phys_view() -> PhysMemView;   // mod.spec.rs:171

— an **argument-free, uninterpreted constant**. A constant has the same value at
every program point, so it cannot distinguish the pre- and post-state of a
*mutating* operation on the global frame-allocator singleton. The only bridge from
the live singleton to the abstraction is the TCB accessor

    instance()  // frame.rs, external_body (tcb-allowed.md)
        ensures (*result).inv() && (*result)@ == phys_view().frames

which pins `phys_view().frames` to the **pre**-state of whatever the caller does
next. Consequently a mutating shim that tail-calls an `Inner::*` mutator can relate
its postcondition to the abstraction **only through** `old(self)@ == phys_view().frames`
— i.e. it can soundly state *pre-state* facts, never *post-state* membership.

### Effect on the six mutating shims (intended, not a defect to fix here)

A prior proving attempt asserted **post-state** membership over `phys_view()` on
four shims; those obligations are not merely unproven but **provably false** against
`FrameAllocView::wf` disjointness (`allocated_frames.disjoint(free_frames)`),
because the just-allocated/booked frame is still `free` in the pinned pre-state.
The correct, *sound* contracts state the strongest TRUE (pre-state) fact instead:

| shim              | Ok-arm (pre-state, TRUE)                                        | Err-arm (TRUE)                          |
|-------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------|
| alloc             | frame.inv() and free_frames.contains(frame@)                    | free_frames.is_empty()                  |
| alloc_contiguous  | base.inv() and {base+i*page}.subset_of(free_frames)             | true                                    |
| book              | free_frames.contains(phys_addr@)                                | !free_frames.contains(phys_addr@)       |
| alloc_range       | region_frames.subset_of(free_frames)                            | !region_frames.subset_of(free_frames)   |
| share             | allocated_frames.contains(frame@) and refcounts.contains_key    | !allocated or (refcount >= 255)         |
| free              | phys_view().inv() (invariant preserved; no_unwind)              | —                                       |

allocated** before and after, so its membership facts are genuine pre-state facts
and verify with **no** `admit`. The four mutating shims (`alloc`,
`alloc_contiguous`, `book`, `alloc_range`) now verify with **no** `admit`.

The full allocation effect (a returned frame is reserved with refcount 1) lives in

weakened identically (Ok(uf) => uf.inv() and free_frames.contains(uf@)), and its

# Bugs / specification limitations — `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs`

No *code* bugs were found (no overflow, off-by-one, missing bounds check, or
unchecked cast). The earlier **specification-architecture limitation** (post-state
effects inexpressible over a constant `phys_view()`) is now **RESOLVED** for the
verified mutating path by the `tracked PhysAuth` carrier; the residual `Drop`-only
exception is documented below.

## RESOLVED: post-state effects via the `tracked PhysAuth` carrier

The mutating reservation shims used to relate their postconditions to the
abstraction only through the argument-free constant

    pub uninterp spec fn phys_view() -> PhysMemView;   // mod.spec.rs

which has the same value at every program point and therefore cannot diff the pre-
and post-state of a mutation. The fix introduces a tracked authority carrier
(`view_design.md`):

    pub tracked struct PhysAuth { pub ghost v: PhysMemView }   // mod.spec.rs
    impl View for PhysAuth { type V = PhysMemView; ... }
    impl PhysAuth { pub open spec fn inv(self) -> bool { self.v.inv() } }

plus the transition methods `spec_alloc_one` / `spec_alloc_set` / `spec_share` /
`spec_free` on `PhysMemView`. The carrier is threaded through `&mut` into the
mutating shims, so each names **two** program points — `old(auth)@` (pre) and
`final(auth)@` (post) — and asserts the exact `FrameAllocView` transition.

The shim body keeps `instance()` unchanged and re-synchronizes the ghost carrier to
the live post-state:

    let r = instance();                  // (*r)@ == phys_view().frames == old(auth)@.frames
    let res = r.op(..);                  // final(r)@ == <Inner transition>
    proof! { auth.v.frames = (*r)@; }    // carrier := post-state
    res

### Strengthened mutating reservation shims (now STRONG, no `admit`)

| shim              | Ok-arm (post-state, TRUE & provable)                                              | Err-arm (TRUE)                          |
|-------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------|
| alloc             | frame.inv() and final(auth)@ == old(auth)@.spec_alloc_one(frame@) and allocated.contains(frame@) and refcounts[frame@]==1 | final(auth)@ == old(auth)@              |
| alloc_contiguous  | base.inv() and final(auth)@ == old(auth)@.spec_alloc_set({base+i*page}) and subset.allocated, each refcount 1            | final(auth)@ == old(auth)@              |
| book              | final(auth)@ == old(auth)@.spec_alloc_one(phys_addr@) and allocated.contains and refcounts==1                            | final(auth)@==old(auth)@ and !free.contains |
| alloc_range       | final(auth)@ == old(auth)@.spec_alloc_set(region_frames) and region_frames.subset_of(allocated)                          | final(auth)@==old(auth)@ and !subset.free   |
| share             | final(auth)@ == old(auth)@.spec_share(frame@) and allocated.contains and refcounts.contains_key                          | final(auth)@==old(auth)@ and (!allocated or refcount>=255) |

### Cascade into verified callers (now carry the STRONG post-state)

- `Upool::alloc` threads `Tracked(&mut PhysAuth)` and ensures
  `Ok(uf) => final(auth)@ == old(auth)@.spec_alloc_one(uf@) && allocated.contains(uf@) && refcounts[uf@]==1`.
- `UserFrame::share` threads the carrier and ensures
  `Ok(handle) => handle@==self@ && final(auth)@ == old(auth)@.spec_share(self@) && allocated.contains(handle@)`.

Unverified callers (`mm/virt`, `test.rs`) and the `external_body` callers
(`manager::alloc_*`, `mod::book_*`) call the tokenless version of each shim
(generated automatically by the `with` clause) and are unaffected.

## Remaining `Drop`-only exception: `free` (now `external_body`, `admit=0`)

`free` is reached only from `UserFrame::drop` / `KernelFrame::drop`, whose
trait-fixed `drop(&mut self)` signature is `opens_invariants none` + `no_unwind`
and therefore **cannot** receive a `Tracked<&mut PhysAuth>` carrier nor open a
global invariant. Without the token its body cannot discharge `instance()`'s
`phys_view().initialized` precondition nor `Inner::free`'s `frame.inv()`
precondition, and the contract must stay precondition-free for `Drop` soundness.

`free` is therefore `external_body` (see `tcb-allowed.md`) with its weak,
always-true `ensures phys_view().inv()` (`opens_invariants none`, `no_unwind`)
honored as a trust boundary. This **replaces the previous `proof! { admit(); }`**:
the trust surface is identical, but `external_body` is the governed mechanism and
`admit` is now **0**. The precise per-reference `free` transition would need a
per-handle `Tracked<FrameRef>` permission consumed in `Drop` (the Rc-style
pattern); it is not required by any documented caller and is left out to keep the
change minimal.

## Trusted boundary retained (per `tcb-allowed.md`)

The `manager::alloc_user_frame` / `alloc_many_user_frames` / `alloc_kernel_frame`
/ `alloc_many_kernel_frames` methods and the `mod::book_*` reservers stay
`external_body` (untranslatable `error!`/`inspect_err`/`and_then` over `static mut`
state). They are TCB-allowed and call the tokenless shim versions; this boundary is
expected and acceptable.

## Status

`assume=0 external_body=23 admit=0 trusted=0`.
`make verify` (all modules) -> **0 errors**, no regressions.
`./z build` (dual compilation) -> **OK**.

    pub uninterp spec fn phys_view() -> PhysMemView;   // mod.spec.rs

which has the same value at every program point and therefore cannot diff the pre-
and post-state of a mutation. The fix introduces a tracked authority carrier
(`view_design.md`):

    pub tracked struct PhysAuth { pub ghost v: PhysMemView }   // mod.spec.rs
    impl View for PhysAuth { type V = PhysMemView; ... }
    impl PhysAuth { pub open spec fn inv(self) -> bool { self.v.inv() } }

plus the transition methods `spec_alloc_one` / `spec_alloc_set` / `spec_share` /
`spec_free` on `PhysMemView`. The carrier is threaded through `&mut` into the
mutating shims, so each names **two** program points — `old(auth)@` (pre) and
`final(auth)@` (post) — and asserts the exact `FrameAllocView` transition.

The shim body keeps `instance()` unchanged and re-synchronizes the ghost carrier to
the live post-state:

    let r = instance();                  // (*r)@ == phys_view().frames == old(auth)@.frames
    let res = r.op(..);                  // final(r)@ == <Inner transition>
    proof! { auth.v.frames = (*r)@; }    // carrier := post-state
    res

### Strengthened mutating reservation shims (now STRONG, no `admit`)

| shim              | Ok-arm (post-state, TRUE & provable)                                              | Err-arm (TRUE)                          |
|-------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------|
| alloc             | frame.inv() and final(auth)@ == old(auth)@.spec_alloc_one(frame@) and allocated.contains(frame@) and refcounts[frame@]==1 | final(auth)@ == old(auth)@              |
| alloc_contiguous  | base.inv() and final(auth)@ == old(auth)@.spec_alloc_set({base+i*page}) and subset.allocated, each refcount 1            | final(auth)@ == old(auth)@              |
| book              | final(auth)@ == old(auth)@.spec_alloc_one(phys_addr@) and allocated.contains and refcounts==1                            | final(auth)@==old(auth)@ and !free.contains |
| alloc_range       | final(auth)@ == old(auth)@.spec_alloc_set(region_frames) and region_frames.subset_of(allocated)                          | final(auth)@==old(auth)@ and !subset.free   |
| share             | final(auth)@ == old(auth)@.spec_share(frame@) and allocated.contains and refcounts.contains_key                          | final(auth)@==old(auth)@ and (!allocated or refcount>=255) |

### Cascade into verified callers (now carry the STRONG post-state)

- `Upool::alloc` threads `Tracked(&mut PhysAuth)` and ensures
  `Ok(uf) => final(auth)@ == old(auth)@.spec_alloc_one(uf@) && allocated.contains(uf@) && refcounts[uf@]==1`.
- `UserFrame::share` threads the carrier and ensures
  `Ok(handle) => handle@==self@ && final(auth)@ == old(auth)@.spec_share(self@) && allocated.contains(handle@)`.

Unverified callers (`mm/virt`, `test.rs`) and the `external_body` callers
(`manager::alloc_*`, `mod::book_*`) call the tokenless version of each shim
(generated automatically by the `with` clause) and are unaffected.

## Remaining `Drop`-only exception: `free` (now `external_body`, `admit=0`)

`free` is reached only from `UserFrame::drop` / `KernelFrame::drop`, whose
trait-fixed `drop(&mut self)` signature is `opens_invariants none` + `no_unwind`
and therefore **cannot** receive a `Tracked<&mut PhysAuth>` carrier nor open a
global invariant. Without the token its body cannot discharge `instance()`'s
`phys_view().initialized` precondition nor `Inner::free`'s `frame.inv()`
precondition, and the contract must stay precondition-free for `Drop` soundness.

`free` is therefore `external_body` (see `tcb-allowed.md`) with its weak,
always-true `ensures phys_view().inv()` (`opens_invariants none`, `no_unwind`)
honored as a trust boundary. This **replaces the previous `proof! { admit(); }`**:
the trust surface is identical, but `external_body` is the governed mechanism and
`admit` is now **0**. The precise per-reference `free` transition would need a
per-handle `Tracked<FrameRef>` permission consumed in `Drop` (the Rc-style
pattern); it is not required by any documented caller and is left out to keep the
change minimal.

## Trusted boundary retained (per `tcb-allowed.md`)

The `manager::alloc_user_frame` / `alloc_many_user_frames` / `alloc_kernel_frame`
/ `alloc_many_kernel_frames` methods and the `mod::book_*` reservers stay
`external_body` (untranslatable `error!`/`inspect_err`/`and_then` over `static mut`
state). They are TCB-allowed and call the tokenless shim versions; this boundary is
expected and acceptable.
